subject: Re: Benchmark report FAQ — EMEA data residency + region comparisons wording
body:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 09:12 AM CET
Subject: Benchmark report FAQ — EMEA data residency + region comparisons wording
Attachments: Benchmark_Report_FAQ_v7_(working).docx; Landing_Page_Wirecopy_v4_(benchmarks).docx

Hi Wei / Soojin,

Quick EMEA pass before we lock the FAQ + landing copy.

EU enterprise prospects (esp. Germany/France) will read the benchmark tables and immediately ask two things:

1) Data residency: “If I select EU, is anything ever routed out of the EU?”
2) Region comparisons: “Can I use the table to conclude EU is ‘better/worse’ than US?” (We need to avoid over-claiming; also network distance can dominate.)

Right now the FAQ wording is a bit ambiguous on (1) because it mentions fallback/routing without stating the controls. I’m worried we’ll create a support + security fire drill during launch week.

Request:
- Add an explicit FAQ entry (or tighten the existing one) with language that works for EU procurement + security. It should clearly distinguish:
  - Hosted API region selection behavior
  - Dedicated/Private options for strict residency
  - What “fallback” means (and that it can be constrained by policy / customer config)
- Add a “How to interpret cross-region differences” note that makes it clear results are reported per region and should not be treated as a universal ranking.

Michael: can you also sanity check the residency language so we don’t accidentally promise something we can’t guarantee in every deployment mode?

Thanks,
Lukas

—
Lukas Meyer
EMEA Field Alignment | Redwood Inference



From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 11:01 AM CET
Subject: Re: Benchmark report FAQ — EMEA data residency + region comparisons wording

Got it. Proposed edits below (draft text; happy to tune tone).

A) New FAQ entry (Data residency / where requests are processed)

Q: If I choose an EU region, will my requests ever be processed outside the EU?
A: When you explicitly select an EU region, Redwood processes requests in that region. For strict data residency requirements, Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private support region-locked deployments and customer-managed networking controls. Some resiliency features (e.g., multi-region failover) are optional and can be configured to remain within a geographic boundary.

B) Tighten existing “fallback” mention

Replace: “Redwood may route requests to compatible capacity when constrained.”
With: “Routing and fallback behavior is policy-driven. Customers can restrict routing to specific regions/capacity tiers based on their requirements.”

C) Add interpretability note (cross-region comparisons)

Q: Can I compare regions directly using the benchmark tables?
A: The report publishes results per region using the same benchmark harness and configuration, but cross-region end-to-end latency for your application will also depend on client-to-region network distance and request patterns. Use the per-region results to evaluate performance within the region(s) relevant to your users.

Michael—please flag any “too absolute” phrasing. Lukas—if you have a preferred “procurement-safe” sentence for Dedicated/Private, send it and I’ll incorporate.

Wei



From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 12:26 PM CET
Subject: Re: Benchmark report FAQ — EMEA data residency + region comparisons wording

Edits from Legal lens (mainly to avoid hard guarantees in Hosted API without the appropriate qualifier):

1) Change “Redwood processes requests in that region” → “Redwood is designed to process requests in the region you select.”

2) Add one clarifying sentence that we don’t include customer data in the benchmark dataset (since this gets conflated in residency conversations):
- “The benchmark results in this report are generated from synthetic/internal prompt sets and do not include customer request logs.”

3) On “optional failover” wording: good direction, but I’d avoid implying we always support “geographic boundary” constraints in all default SKUs. Suggest:
- “Some resiliency features (e.g., failover) are optional and can be configured based on your requirements; for strict residency, Redwood Dedicated/Private can be deployed with region-locked controls.”

4) Cross-region comparison answer looks fine. Minor addition:
- “We do not recommend using cross-region differences in this report as a proxy for your user-perceived latency unless your clients are similarly located.”

If we want to be extra safe, we can add: “See your contract / order form for the specific deployment configuration.” (Up to you; sometimes marketing hates this.)

Michael Grant
Legal | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly what we need.

Two field-driven tweaks (for EU procurement conversations):

- In the residency answer, can we explicitly say “region-locked” once? Buyers will search for that phrase.
- Add one sentence clarifying that “routing/fallback” is not the same thing as “data sharing” (they assume we’re replicating prompts everywhere).

Maybe:
“Routing policies control where requests are served; they do not require sharing your prompts with third parties.”

Wei: can you fold Michael’s edits + the above into the FAQ doc and ping Ben/Elliot if landing copy needs a matching line?

Ben: once updated, I’ll send to Stephanie (NA) as well so we don’t end up with two versions of the answer.

Lukas

Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:03 AM CET
Subject: Re: Benchmark report FAQ — EMEA data residency + region comparisons wording

Done. I updated the working FAQ doc and left track-changes notes.

Final text (compressed):

Q: If I choose an EU region, will my requests ever be processed outside the EU?
A: Redwood is designed to process requests in the region you select. Routing and fallback behavior is policy-driven, and customers can restrict routing to specific regions/capacity tiers based on their requirements. For strict data residency requirements, Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private support region-locked deployments and customer-managed networking controls. The benchmark results in this report are generated from synthetic/internal prompt sets and do not include customer request logs.

Q: Can I compare regions directly using the benchmark tables?
A: The report publishes results per region using the same benchmark harness and configuration, but cross-region end-to-end latency for your application will also depend on client-to-region network distance and request patterns. We do not recommend using cross-region differences in this report as a proxy for user-perceived latency unless your clients are similarly located.

Ben/Soojin: if you want, I can add a 1-line version of the residency sentence for the landing page FAQ (less text).

Wei
